about: Fresh recognition ratings for revised connections (2026-10-13), by a pass that did not write the revisions. Replaces the pre-revision audit entry for these ids.

PLX-BCH-008.note: Chemical names add one step but the A/D/E/K set is a well-known list once retinol and tocopherol are recognized.

PLX-BCH-011.note: Requires recalling a cofactor for each enzyme; lysyl oxidase and tyrosinase point toward copper/Menkes for prepared students.

PLX-BCH-022.note: Must separate from cystic fibrosis, which shares bronchiectasis, sinusitis and male infertility; players may expect situs inversus.

PLX-BCH-024.note: GM2 ganglioside plus cherry-red macula and onion-skin lysosomes identify Tay-Sachs immediately.

PLX-BCH-026.note: Bone crises with AVN and hepatosplenomegaly is the well-known Gaucher pattern.

PLX-BCH-028.note: Arylsulfatase A deficiency names the disease outright.

PLX-BCH-029.note: Hyperextensible skin with atrophic scars is the textbook EDS picture.

PLX-BCH-030.note: Low copper and ceruloplasmin suggest Wilson disease; hypotonia and hypopigmentation in an infant are needed to land on Menkes.

PLX-BCH-032.note: Four B vitamins; recalling the PDH cofactor mnemonic is quick, though plain 'B vitamins' is an easy surface guess.

PLX-BCH-034.note: Looks like the counterregulatory hormones, so players may expect growth hormone; thyroid hormone distinguishes the PEPCK framing.

PLX-BCH-051.note: Sweet-smelling urine with elevated branched-chain amino acids is pathognomonic for MSUD.

PLX-BCH-054.note: Ringed sideroblasts gives it away; microcytosis fits hereditary forms, whereas acquired sideroblastic anemia is often normo- or macrocytic.

PLX-BCH-055.note: All four are classic CYP450 inducers, so players must decide between the inducer group and porphyria precipitants.

PLX-BCH-057.note: Night blindness and Bitot spots point straight to vitamin A.

PLX-BCH-059.note: Rachitic rosary and bowed legs are the classic rickets set.

PLX-BCH-060.note: Wernicke and Korsakoff instantly signal thiamine deficiency.

PLX-BCH-061.note: Hartnup disease and carcinoid syndrome together immediately suggest tryptophan/niacin.

PLX-BCH-063.note: Three tiles also fit folate deficiency; subacute combined degeneration is the deciding tile, but most students find it quickly.

PLX-BCH-064.note: Each enzyme is better known for another association; recalling zinc as the shared cofactor takes real retrieval.

PLX-BCH-079.note: Lysosomal storage disease is the obvious link; the ERT framing is less obvious and other diseases (e.g. Hunter, Niemann-Pick B) also have ERT.

CARD-008.note: Pulmonary fibrosis plus blue-gray skin is the well-known amiodarone pattern.

CARD-014.note: Emotional stress in a postmenopausal woman with clean coronaries is classic Takotsubo.

CARD-016.note: Megaesophagus, megacolon and a reduviid vector make Chagas instant.

CARD-018.note: Rib notching with arm-leg pressure discrepancy is classic coarctation.

CARD-019.note: The SAD triad plus pulsus parvus is a widely memorized set.

CARD-020.note: Eponymous peripheral signs and the diastolic decrescendo murmur quickly identify aortic regurgitation.

CARD-021.note: An apical diastolic rumble with loud S1, LA enlargement and atrial fibrillation is the standard mitral stenosis set.

CARD-022.note: Papillary muscle rupture pulls toward MI complications; players must recognize the MR theme across finding and cause.

CARD-028.note: Egg-on-string radiograph identifies TGA immediately for most students.

CARD-034.note: Beck triad elements plus pulsus paradoxus are an instantly recognized tamponade set.

CARD-035.note: Requires reasoning that each causes bleeding into the pericardium rather than serous effusion.

CARD-036.note: Uremia and Dressler syndrome are a well-known pericarditis cause set.

CARD-037.note: Rupture and mural thrombus tiles make the post-MI complication theme quick.

CARD-040.note: Each drug is known for other uses; linking them requires recalling vasoconstrictive coronary effects.

CARD-042.note: Varicose veins and hemosiderin staining make venous insufficiency obvious.

DERM-006.note: Herpetic whitlow and dendritic keratitis immediately point to herpes simplex.

DERM-007.note: All four are named VZV syndromes, and herpes zoster ophthalmicus and Ramsay Hunt are themselves forms of shingles, so the tiles overlap.

DERM-019.note: Mixed tile types and shared links to SJS/TEN and viral exanthems require discriminating the DRESS pattern.

DERM-029.note: Silvery plaques and Auspitz sign are instant psoriasis clues.

ENDO-011.note: PTU plus potassium iodide makes thyroid storm treatment quick to spot.

ENDO-020.note: Stones, bones, groans and psychiatric overtones is a classic mnemonic list.

ENDO-021.note: Standard PTH actions taught as a set; phosphaturia and 1-alpha-hydroxylase together point to PTH.

ENDO-034.note: Hypertension with hypokalemia suggests 17-hydroxylase deficiency or hyperaldosteronism; elevated androgens and 11-deoxycortisol are needed to decide.

ENDO-041.note: Four well-known sulfonylureas, a straightforward drug-class list; glimepiride fits equally.

ENDO-042.note: Four diabetes drugs; players must exclude weight-gaining or neutral agents rather than simply group antidiabetics.

GI-004.note: These diseases share many links (autoimmunity, GI disease), so the oral-ulcer theme takes thought; reactive arthritis or HIV could also be expected.

GI-013.note: Pernicious anemia and Diphyllobothrium latum make B12 deficiency obvious.

GI-025.note: MCP arthropathy with diabetes and cardiomyopathy is the classic hemochromatosis set.

GI-029.note: Caput medusae with ascites and splenomegaly identifies portal hypertension quickly.

GI-031.note: Atazanavir requires knowing its UGT1A1 inhibition; the others share the conjugation-defect mechanism.

GI-032.note: Three tiles end in 'jaundice', which reveals the neonatal jaundice group without reasoning.

GI-040.note: Diverse drug classes linked only by recalling pancreatitis as an adverse effect.

GI-041.note: Pseudocyst gives the pancreatitis theme away; hypocalcemia confirms.

GI-053.note: Acanthocytes with reduced ApoB lipoproteins identify abetalipoproteinemia.

GI-054.note: Each tile has a stronger alternate association; the lead-point link needs recall of intussusception causes.

GI-059.note: Erythema nodosum with pyoderma gangrenosum and uveitis is the standard IBD extraintestinal list.

GI-060.note: Fecalith and lymphoid hyperplasia quickly suggest appendicitis causes.

GI-061.note: Delayed meconium with explosive stool after rectal exam is classic Hirschsprung.

GI-064.note: Common laxatives; lactulose and PEG together signal osmotic agents.

PLEXUS-GEN-002.note: Two '-tecan' drugs plus etoposide quickly suggest topoisomerase inhibitors; doxorubicin is the less obvious member.

PLEXUS-GEN-007.note: Orotic aciduria with normal ammonia is the classic distinction from OTC deficiency, which is well taught.

PLEXUS-GEN-010.note: Ataxia with radiation hypersensitivity and elevated AFP identifies ataxia-telangiectasia.

PLEXUS-GEN-015.note: Lisch nodules and neurofibromas are pathognomonic NF1 clues.

PLEXUS-GEN-016.note: Hyperphagia with hypotonia and hypogonadism points quickly to Prader-Willi.

PLX-HEM-003.note: Factors IX and VIII point straight to the aPTT arm; prekallikrein and HMWK need a moment, and players may expect factors XI or XII.

PLX-HEM-006.note: Primaquine plus sulfonamides is the classic G6PD trigger list; fava beans and dapsone are equally expected members.

PLX-HEM-010.note: LDH, haptoglobin and reticulocytes are the textbook hemolysis panel and are recognized instantly.

PLX-HEM-011.note: A well-known MAHA list; HUS is the obvious missing member that players may expect.

PLX-HEM-013.note: "Sickled erythrocytes" names the disease outright, so the other three are sorted around it instantly.

PLX-HEM-019.note: Burton line is a near-giveaway, but wrist drop and colic need the lead link recalled; cognitive impairment is generic.

PLX-HEM-020.note: Basophilic stippling and ALA dehydratase are classic lead clues; ringed sideroblasts and ZPP also suggest other sideroblastic or iron disorders.

PLX-HEM-024.note: Transfusional iron overload and marrow expansion point quickly to thalassemia major, though HbF and target cells overlap with sickle cell disease.

PLX-HEM-036.note: Ristocetin cofactor activity gives it away; the hedged "Possibly" tile reads oddly and stands out from the other three.

PLX-HEM-041.note: The yolk sac-liver-spleen-marrow sequence is a classic mnemonic set and is recognized instantly.

PLX-HEM-045.note: Cytarabine, gemcitabine and azacitidine share a "-cit-" look; capecitabine is an equally expected member.

PLX-HEM-052.note: Low LAP and basophilia are classic CML tells, though left shift and splenomegaly need discrimination from leukemoid reactions.

PLX-HEM-053.note: t(15;17) and ATRA responsiveness are instant APL identifiers.

PLX-HEM-054.note: Reed-Sternberg cells name the disease outright.

PLX-HEM-055.note: Starry-sky histology and endemic jaw involvement are instant Burkitt identifiers.

PLX-HEM-056.note: TRAP positivity is a one-word giveaway for hairy cell leukemia.

PLX-HEM-057.note: Richter transformation is CLL-specific and gives the group away, although CD5 also suggests mantle cell lymphoma.

PLX-HEM-061.note: Bence Jones and cast nephropathy point immediately to myeloma; the light-chain framing adds little extra reasoning.

PLX-HEM-063.note: Aquagenic pruritus with low EPO is a classic PV pair; erythromelalgia also suggests essential thrombocythemia.

PLX-HEM-064.note: Dacrocytes plus leukoerythroblastosis is the textbook myelofibrosis picture, though massive splenomegaly also suggests CML.

IMM-002.note: Delayed umbilical cord separation is an instant LAD identifier.

IMM-006.note: CD8 and beta-2 microglobulin point straight to MHC class I; the main challenge is separating it from a class II group.

IMM-007.note: The HLA-DP/DQ/DR tile and CD4 identify class II quickly; the challenge is separating it from a class I group.

IMM-009.note: CD19 and CD21 signal B cells; CD20 and surface IgM are equally expected members.

IMM-020.note: All four end in "vaccine", so the group is easy to spot; separating non-live from live vaccines takes some recall, and injected influenza or rabies vaccines fit equally well.

IMM-022.note: Absent B cells with enteroviral infection is a classic XLA picture, though reduced immunoglobulins alone fits other humoral deficiencies.

IMM-024.note: "IgA" appears in two tiles, and anaphylactic transfusion reactions give the diagnosis away.

IMM-025.note: High IgM with low switched isotypes points directly to hyper-IgM syndrome; Pneumocystis adds the T-cell link.

IMM-026.note: Retained primary teeth and cold abscesses are the FATED mnemonic and give Job syndrome away instantly.

IMM-027.note: Eczema, infections and small platelets form the WATER triad and are recognized instantly; two tiles both describe platelets.

IMM-030.note: Serum sickness and the Arthus reaction are the textbook type III examples, and "immune-complex" in a tile states the mechanism.

IMM-035.note: Onset within minutes points straight to hyperacute rejection; the vascular lesions need discrimination from vasculitis or TMA.

IMM-040.note: Infliximab and adalimumab are the archetypal anti-TNF drugs; three share "-mab", and golimumab fits equally.

MICRO-014.note: Growth on BCYE agar identifies Legionella instantly.

MICRO-016.note: Saber shins and the Hutchinson triad members point to congenital syphilis, but saddle nose and deafness overlap with GPA and congenital rubella; Hutchinson teeth is the expected missing member.

MICRO-021.note: Halo sign and galactomannan are well-known Aspergillus clues; the cavitating nodule and hemoptysis tiles overlap with TB and GPA.

MICRO-035.note: Players must reason about larval transmission from food, and Taenia saginata or Clonorchis would fit equally; T. solium can also cause cysticercosis by egg ingestion, which may give some players pause.

MICRO-036.note: Dog-sheep transmission and daughter cysts point to Echinococcus quickly.

MICRO-045.note: Endemic Burkitt and nasopharyngeal carcinoma are the classic EBV cancers; Hodgkin lymphoma is an expected member that is missing.

MICRO-048.note: PDA, salt-and-pepper retinopathy and deafness are the familiar rubella findings, though the blueberry-muffin rash and deafness overlap with CMV.

MICRO-053.note: Osler nodes, Roth spots and splinter hemorrhages are the classic endocarditis set; Janeway lesions are the expected member that is missing.

MSK-004.note: A classic urate-raising drug list; loop diuretics and cyclosporine are equally expected members.

MSK-011.note: Hydralazine and isoniazid are classic drug-induced lupus causes; procainamide is the most expected member and is missing.

MSK-013.note: Dry eyes plus dry mouth is recognized as Sjogren syndrome instantly.

MSK-017.note: Four letters of the CREST mnemonic plus anti-centromere are recognized instantly.

MSK-018.note: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with noncaseating granulomas is the instant sarcoidosis pairing.

MSK-021.note: Jaw claudication with temporal headache identifies giant cell arteritis instantly.

MSK-022.note: Upper airway, lung and kidney together form the classic GPA triad, though each tile alone is less specific.

NEPH-004.note: Hydrochlorothiazide gives the class away, though indapamide and metolazone require recall that they are thiazide-like.

NEPH-007.note: Hypoalbuminemia, edema and hyperlipidemia are the defining nephrotic features and are recognized instantly.

NEPH-012.note: Subepithelial humps are a near-giveaway, though low C3 and granular staining also fit lupus nephritis and MPGN.

NEPH-018.note: Sickle cell, analgesics and diabetes make up the classic papillary necrosis mnemonic; acute pyelonephritis is an equally expected member.

NEPH-021.note: Three tiles share a numeric above/below threshold format that marks them as a set, and FENa below 1% gives prerenal away.

NEPH-028.note: Diarrhea, acetazolamide and RTA are standard normal anion gap acidosis causes from the HARDASS mnemonic.

NEPH-031.note: Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules identify diabetic nephropathy instantly.

NEU-002.note: Hyperreflexia, spasticity and an extensor plantar response are the textbook UMN signs; clonus is an equally expected member.

NEU-003.note: Fasciculations, atrophy and hyporeflexia are the textbook LMN signs; the only challenge is separating them from a UMN group.

NEU-006.note: Needs rule-of-4 recall across brainstem levels; "medial" appears in two tiles, and the abducens or oculomotor nuclei would fit equally.

NEU-008.note: Broca area and primary motor cortex make the frontal lobe link quick; prefrontal cortex is an equally expected member.

NEU-012.note: Oligoclonal bands and Dawson fingers identify MS instantly.

NEU-018.note: Ptosis, a dilated pupil and "down and out" eye movement are the textbook CN III palsy findings.

NEU-023.note: These are standard visual-pathway stations behind the chiasm; the parietal (dorsal) optic radiation is an equally expected member.

NEU-024.note: These are standard conductive hearing loss causes; cholesteatoma is an equally expected member.

NEU-026.note: BPPV, vestibular neuritis and Meniere disease are the textbook peripheral vertigo list.

NEU-027.note: Dix-Hallpike plus Epley names BPPV instantly.

NEU-029.note: Rosenthal fibers with a cystic cerebellar mass is a classic giveaway.

NEU-033.note: EBV plus DLBCL plus CD20 points to PCNSL with little thought.

NEU-036.note: Crossed pain-temperature loss with ipsilateral/contralateral wording signals Wallenberg at once.

NEU-038.note: Skull-dura location and lucid interval give epidural hematoma away.

NEU-039.note: Bridging veins and dura-arachnoid location are textbook subdural.

NEU-040.note: Xanthochromia and vasospasm point to SAH quickly; meningismus adds mild ambiguity with meningitis.

NEU-047.note: Vertical gaze palsy and convergence-retraction nystagmus are well-known Parinaud clues.

NEU-049.note: The four dopamine pathways are a memorized set; tile format alone sorts them.

NEU-050.note: Plaques and tangles name Alzheimer instantly.

NEU-056.note: Classic reversible-dementia workup list; normal pressure hydrocephalus and thiamine deficiency fit equally well.

NEU-061.note: Recognizable seizure types; tonic and clonic seizures also qualify, so the set is one choice among several.

PHARM-004.note: The HAVe 1 M&M mnemonic makes the Gq set instant; V1 is an alternate member.

PHARM-005.note: Must separate Gs from Gq/Gi receptors; H2 is an equally common Gs member.

PSY-007.note: Cataplexy plus hypnagogic hallucinations gives narcolepsy at once.

PSY-009.note: Lanugo anchors anorexia; other tiles are broadly associated but the set is quickly recognized.

PSY-012.note: Four familiar SSRIs; any student sorts these instantly.

PSY-014.note: Familiar TCA names, two sharing -ipramine, make this immediate.

PSY-021.note: Nephrogenic DI plus hypothyroidism cues lithium quickly.

PSY-023.note: Lead-pipe rigidity cues NMS over serotonin syndrome; hyperthermia, a cardinal feature, is the expected missing member.

REPRO-001.note: Familiar Wolffian derivatives (SEED mnemonic); vas deferens is the expected alternate.

REPRO-002.note: Recognized neural crest list; 'Peripheral neurons' is broad since somatic motor neurons are not neural crest-derived.

REPRO-013.note: Cocaine plus trauma plus preeclampsia points to abruption quickly.

REPRO-015.note: Requires recognizing the shared unopposed-estrogen mechanism across varied tiles.

REPRO-023.note: Must separate Category 4 from lesser categories; smoking age 35+ and breast cancer also fit.

REPRO-024.note: Absent cremasteric reflex with high-riding testis is classic torsion.

PULM-001.note: Classic pulmonary-toxicity drug list; methotrexate is an equally common member.

PULM-008.note: CADET mnemonic set; discriminating right vs left needs only direction recall.

PULM-009.note: Mirrors the right-shift set; carbon monoxide and decreased 2,3-BPG fit equally well.

PULM-013.note: The standard obstructive list; bronchiectasis is an expected alternate.

PULM-016.note: Intercellular bridges and PTHrP point to squamous carcinoma; central mass requires separating from small cell.

PULM-017.note: Pleural plaques plus mesothelioma give asbestos immediately.

bank-easy-02.note: Familiar QT drugs; haloperidol, methadone and class IA agents fit equally.

bank-easy-13.note: Gallstones plus hypertriglyceridemia point to pancreatitis quickly.

bank-easy-15.note: Classic cyanotic CHD list; truncus arteriosus and tricuspid atresia fit equally. Duplicate of bank-migrated-sys-mixed-0003-L1.

bank-medium-03.note: Separating Gi from Gq/Gs needs recall; every tile ends in 'receptor' unlike other receptor sets, and D2 is an expected alternate.

bank-medium-04.note: Cavernous sinus contents are a memorized list; CN tiles signal it.

bank-medium-13.note: EGPA plus helminths points to eosinophilia quickly.

bank-hard-07.note: Wordplay link across unrelated topics needs a moment to notice the shared word.

bank-hard-11.note: Astro/aster stems plus starry and stellate reveal the star theme fast.

bank-expert-03.note: Requires thinking through negative feedback suppression across axes.

bank-expert-05.note: Must reason that each is hormone resistance with compensatory high levels.

bank-migrated-sys-mixed-0003-L1.note: Duplicate of bank-easy-15; classic cyanotic CHD list.

bank-migrated-sys-pulm-0002-L2.note: Familiar exudate causes; pulmonary embolism and rheumatoid arthritis fit equally.

bank-migrated-sys-renal-0002-L4.note: Recognizable glomerular biopsy findings; must match each to disease.

bank-migrated-sys-renal-0003-L2.note: Insulin and albuterol cue potassium shifting quickly.

bank-migrated-sys-renal-0003-L4.note: Two tiles share the 'urine despite serum osmolality' format, signaling an ADH-disorder set.

bank-migrated-sys-neuro-0001-L2.note: Leg weakness with incontinence cues ACA stroke quickly.

bank-migrated-sys-neuro-0001-L4.note: Three tiles end in 'syndrome'; Weber and medial medullary syndromes fit equally.

bank-migrated-sys-neuro-0002-L2.note: Huntington plus rheumatic fever cue chorea quickly; Wilson disease fits equally.

bank-migrated-sys-pharm-0002-L2.note: BPH and pheochromocytoma point to alpha blockers with brief thought.

bank-ext-007.note: Bronchospasm plus angioedema plus hypotension gives anaphylaxis quickly.

bank-ext-008.note: Heberden nodes and osteophytes name OA at once.

bank-ext-021.note: Obesity plus daytime somnolence cue OSA quickly.

bank-ext-025.note: Purple striae plus central obesity is instant Cushing.

bank-ext-027.note: The TICS list is instant; sideroblastic anemia is the expected alternate.

bank-ext-037.note: ADPKD and coarctation cue berry aneurysms; Marfan syndrome is a commonly expected alternate.

bank-ext-084.note: Two polyangiitis tiles plus Churg-Strauss make ANCA vasculitis instant.

bank-ext-090.note: Condom, diaphragm and cap are obvious barrier methods.

bank-ext-096.note: Tiles spell out the HELLP acronym directly.

bank-ext-101.note: Familiar monitored psychiatric drugs; clozapine and lithium cue the link.

bank-ext-112.note: Major skin cancers are an instantly recognized set.
